steps.name: Poor Slum Youth
steps.text: I came to you to help some big shots solve your problems. You won't find a shoddier district in all Kazdel.

steps.name: Poor Slum Youth
steps.text: I have a group of real good workers willing to help build a furnace node. Think about it: with just a supply of power, this district will be able to transform.

steps.name: Poor Slum Youth
steps.text: People will have work to keep themselves fed and won't cause trouble anymore.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: You sound plenty confident. What do you want from me?

steps.name: Poor Slum Youth
steps.text: Steel for the pipes, right in the middle of the district. You can have your people keep an eye on it, if you want.

steps.name: Poor Slum Youth
steps.text: Trust me, you won't recognize this district in three months.

steps.name: Poor Slum Youth
steps.text: You see those guards watching over the steel? Do you believe me now? It's the bosses who ordered the furnace node to be built. There's plenty in it for you, if you work for them.

steps.name: Broken Horn Boss
steps.text: Hmph. And?

steps.name: Poor Slum Youth
steps.text: I want food, enough to feed a decent team of workers. I know you guys have plenty.

steps.name: Poor Slum Youth
steps.text: Bring it to the warehouse there. We'll have enough space.

steps.name: Poor Slum Youth
steps.text: Trust me, this is a good deal for you.

steps.name: Poor Slum Youth
steps.text: You see the food in this warehouse? Come help build the furnace, and everyone gets some every day. Better than robbing people on the streets. At least you don't have to worry about getting your skull split open.

steps.name: Fierce Mercenary
steps.text: You've got guts, kid. You want to hire mercenaries to work for you?

steps.name: Poor Slum Youth
steps.text: You're big, tough, and not afraid to break a sweat. You'll make great workers.

steps.name: Poor Slum Youth
steps.text: Listen to me, and I'll make sure you all do well for yourselves—better than you're doing right now, at least.
7:40 A.M. \ Overcast

steps.name: Gaunt Sarkaz
steps.text: Good morning, Big Head! Came to get your clothes? Your collar would've been charred, if you came any later.

steps.name: Returned Mercenary
steps.text: Don't you dare call me Big Head. And put away all that crap you picked up. Don't *Sarkaz expletive* pile shit up in front of my door!

steps.name: Gaunt Sarkaz
steps.text: Just one night. I'm selling it to the boiler guy later. Won't bother you, not that much, anyway.

steps.name: Gaunt Sarkaz
steps.text: The hoodlums would have stolen them if I left them at home. But no one in these parts would dare have their finger in your pie.

steps.name: Returned Mercenary
steps.text: You're talkative today. Aren't you going to work?

steps.name: Gaunt Sarkaz
steps.text: Didn't you hear that nasty noise last night? A rock THIS big fell right on top of the construction site.

steps.name: Gaunt Sarkaz
steps.text: If I went to work now, I'd have to help move the rock and fill in the crater... why would I want to do three times the work for the same amount of food? Say, you're up early, are you going somewhere?

steps.name: Returned Mercenary
steps.text: No, just in the mood for a morning stroll.

steps.name: Gaunt Sarkaz
steps.text: Well, don't go to the south side. It's a mess.

steps.name: Gaunt Sarkaz
steps.text: I was out there cutting wires in the morning when I heard that a hunk of iron fell from the sky, straight through somebody's roof. They hardly started grinning when the Broken Horns showed up.

steps.name: Gaunt Sarkaz
steps.text: Now there's a handful of gangs wanting to trade that iron for food. Everybody wants a big piece and they're almost fighting over it.

steps.name: Returned Mercenary
steps.text: Over iron? Is it valuable?

steps.name: Gaunt Sarkaz
steps.text: Oriron isn't valuable only when burdenbeasts fly.

steps.name: Gaunt Sarkaz
steps.text: Those Broken Horn hardheads would draw their blades for half a hunk of black brick. They'd've torn the house down if the Consultant wasn't there to keep them in line.

steps.name: Returned Mercenary
steps.text: Well, they'll stay in line with the Consultant watching them.

steps.name: Gaunt Sarkaz
steps.text: Don't say I didn't warn you. And I would take the long way round, if I were you. You see those two over there?

steps.name: Returned Mercenary
steps.text: Where?

steps.name: Gaunt Sarkaz
steps.text: You know Nymph. Don't know the other one, but she looks like a Lich.

steps.name: Gaunt Sarkaz
steps.text: Those two were keeping order around here before you came back.

steps.name: Returned Mercenary
steps.text: A Lich? What are they doing here? Isn't she worried about getting her nice shoes dirty?

steps.name: Gaunt Sarkaz
steps.text: Might be Nymphy's friend. Look how they're laughing with each other.

steps.name: Gaunt Sarkaz
steps.text: There's the boiler man! Gotta borrow your cart, Big Head.

steps.name: Returned Mercenary
steps.text: What did you just say?

steps.name: Gaunt Sarkaz
steps.text: I-I mean, Big Guy! Have a nice stroll, I've got junk to sell.

steps.name: Returned Mercenary
steps.text: I'll let it slide this time... if you share half the money you made.

steps.name: Gaunt Sarkaz
steps.text: Huh? Now just wait a second, Big Guy, (*whispers*) it's not like I don't want to share with you, but what's money good for in Kazdel these days?

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: If a revenant fragment is too big, press this red button in the back until the box becomes big enough to hold it.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: And do NOT poke your head inside, no matter what happens. That's pretty much it. There's a manual inside as well. Any questions?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: You really don't have a treasure map that can show revenant fragment locations in real time?

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: I told you, Liches don't grant wishes! Making Arts Creations is serious business.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Here, put this on.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: The Lich Arts inside will detect nearby revenant fragments, and emit an alarm when you're close enough.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: The box looks like a mercenary communicator.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Be glad you got that. I was planning to make the case out of scrap paper.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: But this doesn't look much more serious than a treasure map.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Hey, I was joking! Give it back!

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: I have to keep an eye on the furnace repairs, and review the books that my master gave me. I'm counting on you to find the revenant fragments, Nymph.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Of course! That's what friends are for.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: They were right! You're the kindest, gentlest Djall in all Kazdel!

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Wh-Who says? There aren't that many Djaj in Kazdel. I'm just helping out a friend.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Well, you get back to work. I-I got to go myself!

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Are you sure? Is this where you saw the meteor fall?

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Yes, this is the place.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: But Ermi's detector isn't reacting at all... do you remember what the meteor looked like?

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Some of them were round, some of them bumpy...

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: There was more than one?

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: The wonderful smell when roasted on an open flame...

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Leave the skin on. Soft and fluffy... simply lip-smacking.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Ma'am, what are you talking about?

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Go inside. They're only open in the morning, and they won't stay open for you.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: I'm looking for the meteor, not Mercenary Potatoes! The stuff that the fireworks dropped last night!

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Fried rice? There's no fried rice.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Never mind... I guess I might as well ask the mercenaries.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Get some rest, granny, I'll bring roast potatoes next time.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Thanks. I like mine a little charred.
Nymph keeps walking. The courtyard is not big, but there are a lot of things here.
Mercenaries who back from the front lines have set up camp. Simple ovens bake in a corner, with embers still smoldering inside.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Hello... anybody here?

steps.name: Leisurely Passerby
steps.text: You're too late.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Wh-What?

steps.name: Leisurely Passerby
steps.text: I bought the last bag of roast potatoes. Come back tomorrow.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: I'm not here for potatoes!

steps.name: Leisurely Passerby
steps.text: We've met twice before, but that was during the civil war. I guess you don't remember.

steps.name: Leisurely Passerby
steps.text: The roast potatoes are pretty good. I could give you half a one, if you want.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: No thanks... I'm here for the meteor that fell last night.

steps.name: Leisurely Passerby
steps.text: You're after that piece of iron? Well, it's not here anymore.

steps.name: Leisurely Passerby
steps.text: The Broken Horns didn't get what they wanted at the Veteran's Home, so they got a few gangs together to bring it to their own turf.

steps.name: Leisurely Passerby
steps.text: The commotion lasted all morning, and nobody's mended that hole in the roof.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: You said a few gangs? Did they all touch that... piece of iron?

steps.name: Leisurely Passerby
steps.text: A dozen or so folks must have touched it, maybe a hundred. A few wise guy tried to scrape some Oriron off with their fingernails.

steps.name: Leisurely Passerby
steps.text: Are you shivering? Do you need a potato to warm your hands?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Oh, er, I'm fine.

steps.name: Leisurely Passerby
steps.text: Go on, don't be shy, I can spare that much.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Thanks... you said they went to all that trouble for a rock with some iron. Doesn't that sound a little weird?

steps.name: Leisurely Passerby
steps.text: You think so too? The young Broken Horns seemed really obsessed with the iron. They just wouldn't leave it alone.

steps.name: Leisurely Passerby
steps.text: You have any idea what's going on?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Let me think...

steps.name: Leisurely Passerby
steps.text: Oh, why am I asking you? It's not like you live here.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Yeah, I haven't been to this district in years. I don't know it well... where can I find the Broken Horns?

steps.name: Leisurely Passerby
steps.text: Go straight until the end of the path, turn right, and keep walking until you reach Burningtail Junction, where the cherry trees used to be. You'll see it.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Thanks! Say, what's your name?

steps.name: Leisurely Passerby
steps.text: They call me...

steps.name: Leisurely Passerby
steps.text: Well, you can call me Pohl.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: I'm Nymph!
There is a sudden crack of thunder in the dark sky, but no raindrops fall.
The sound echoes through the walls, rubble and buried pipelines. The thick and heavy shell begins to peel off, revealing the original texture beneath.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Oh dear, look at the time! It's been a pleasure talking to you, but I have to get some veggies from the Vertical Farm. Gotta rush, bye!

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Oh, okay! Bye!
The young Sarkaz carries his shopping bag with his tail and strolls leisurely into the alley, showing no signs of a rush.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Burningtail Junction... cherry tree? I remember the place, but I thought the cherry trees were cut down before the civil war.

steps.name: Odd Passerby
steps.text: I smell fried potatoes. Where are they?

steps.name: Returned Mercenary
steps.text: Here were are. This street still looks the same.

steps.name: Returned Mercenary
steps.text: There used to be a huge piece of Originium crystal here. Did they move it out, or do I remember wrong?

steps.name: Returned Mercenary
steps.text: Bean Sprout said things were bad here, but I haven't seen a single hoodlum yet. I should sock him one when I get back.

steps.name: Returned Mercenary
steps.text: My house is just around the corner. She used to stand guard here, and I'd get a good beating if she caught me running out into the streets.

steps.name: Returned Mercenary
steps.text: What's the point of looking for it, though? It's been so many years. People come and go; somebody else probably lives there now.

steps.name: Returned Mercenary
steps.text: What would they think if I said it used to be my home? They'd probably think I was crazy, or just an idiot. Not like I can come back and reclaim it as mine.

steps.name: Returned Mercenary
steps.text: ...Just a quick look. That'll do.

steps.name: Returned Mercenary
steps.text: Go around the corner and get your look. Then go get something to eat. Just another day.

steps.name: Returned Mercenary
steps.text: Wait, where's the house?

steps.name: Returned Mercenary
steps.text: Just a wall? Where's the roof?

steps.name: Returned Mercenary
steps.text: Who tore down my house?!

steps.name: Mischievous Kid
steps.text: What are you shouting about, silly big guy?

steps.name: Mischievous Kid
steps.text: Shouldn't you go home and roast some potatoes? What are you doing on Broken Horn turf? They'll strip you naked, you know.

steps.name: Returned Mercenary
steps.text: Whose kid are you? Who taught you to talk like that?
The girl in the window does not answer. She makes a face and wags her little head.
The mercenary sees the black rocks growing out of her neck.

steps.name: Returned Mercenary
steps.text: This is Broken Horn turf? How?

steps.name: Mischievous Kid
steps.text: Don't you see the red words on the wall? Oh, don't tell me—you can't read?

steps.name: Mischievous Kid
steps.text: It says, 'TRAITOR'. That's what they say happens to the guys who get on the wrong side of the Broken Horns.

steps.name: Mischievous Kid
steps.text: Hey, don't go! I can teach you, if you want to learn to read. I've got nothing against you Head-Sellers. Hehe.
The mercenary stops in his tracks and turns around, looking up at the girl from below the window.
His yellow, muddled eyes make it difficult to hide much emotion.

steps.name: Returned Mercenary
steps.text: What's a Head-Seller?

steps.name: Mischievous Kid
steps.text: That's what the Broken Horns call people like you, wearing a jacket like that, coming back from the outside.

spans.text: That's what the Broken Horns call people like you, wearing a jacket like that, coming back from the

steps.name: Mischievous Kid
steps.text: But the girl who taught me to read won't let me use that word. She says...

steps.name: Returned Mercenary
steps.text: Where can I find the Broken Horns?
Hey, stop right there! Who are you?

steps.name: Stern Mercenary
steps.text: Two days in the Broken Horns got you blind? I'm here for the gang meeting.

steps.name: Broken Horn Rookie
steps.text: Gang meeting? You? What are you talking about? This isn't your barbecue stall. Since when do cooks get a seat at the table?

steps.name: Stern Mercenary
steps.text: Has your dumb ass healed up? You want me to get the Consultant?

steps.name: Broken Horn Rookie
steps.text: I don't see him anywhere. Where are you gonna find him? Boss says the meeting starts after three bangs on the steel bucket, and no one else gets to go in.

steps.name: Stern Mercenary
steps.text: I'm not deaf. It's only been two bangs.

steps.name: Broken Horn Rookie
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Broken Horn Rookie
steps.text: That's three there.

steps.name: Broken Horn Rookie
steps.text: Heh, you know what, I'll take a little pity on you. You want to go in, give me three roast potatoes tomorrow, and I'm not paying for them.

steps.name: Stern Mercenary
steps.text: Sure. If you dare.

steps.name: Stern Mercenary
steps.text: Take a guess what extra seasoning I'm gonna put on them.

steps.name: Broken Horn Rookie
steps.text: Hey, hold it! Did I say you could go in?

steps.name: Broken Horn Rookie
steps.text: What are you looking at? I'm talking to you!

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Me? I'm here to listen...

steps.name: Broken Horn Rookie
steps.text: Get lost! This is no place for you. See this?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Er... a fire poker?

steps.name: Broken Horn Rookie
steps.text: A knife! Made from a horn! It's really sharp!

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Ouch! That must have hurt. Why would you poke your finger like that? Here, I have a bandage...

steps.name: Broken Horn Rookie
steps.text: You—get lost!

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: This should be the place, but how do I get in?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: I've heard that the Broken Horns are a bunch of unruly young kids, and now...

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Come on, Nymph. Think of your friends. Could anyone help?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Not this one, not that one either. This one might have some influence at a gang meeting, but I don't think she's in Kazdel anymore...

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: What about the Consultant? All the gangs in this district listen to him. But I've never seen him, and I don't know where he lives.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: I should just wait here. He's always the one officiating the gang meetings. I'm sure he'll come by.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: ...No one's coming?!

steps.name: Leisurely Voice
steps.text: Are you waiting for someone, Miss Nymph?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Pohl! Did you get your veggies?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: I was a little late. All they had left was sweet potatoes. That farmer's a grumpy one, he doesn't let you pick. It took a lot of sweet-talking to get a few decent-looking ones.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Wow, sweet potatoes can get this big? The ones I know aren't even a third the size.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: The only way to get ones this big is to try your luck at the Vertical Farm, but I hear the farmers keep the best ones for themselves.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Anyway, what are you doing here?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Oh, I was trying my luck to see if I could run into the Consultant here. The Broken Horns won't let me in, but they wouldn't stop me if I was with the Consultant.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: It might not go down quite like that... do you know the Consultant?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: I asked someone to help get in touch with him, but I never got a response.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: So you're waiting for someone you've never met? How would you recognize him?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: That's why I said I was trying my luck. Maybe he'd know me?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Is that piece of iron really so important?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Not just to me. It's important to everyone else here. I have to bring it back to—

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: The Furnace?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Yes! You saw it too? The fireworks last night...

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: They came from the Furnace. But wasn't the appeasement ceremony in progress then? Are we talking about... revenants? But why are you here? What about the Liches?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Huh? You know about all that?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Just my luck, I thought I was imagining things... this is even worse than I thought.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: You've been standing here for a while, right? How many times did they bang the steel bucket?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Three times, I think.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: The gang meeting has started. I shouldn't have spent so much time shopping today.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: It may not be too late. I think they'll wait for the Consultant...

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Fair point. A gang meeting without the Consultant is basically a brawl.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Well, it's your lucky day, Nymph. Or maybe unlucky day. Come on, let's get this trouble all fixed up.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Huh? No, wait! You don't even know what's going on...

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: I'll tell you my theory on the way, and you can correct me, if I'm wrong.

steps.name: Stern Mercenary
steps.text: Beastshit! No goddamned way!

steps.name: Stern Mercenary
steps.text: That courtyard was given to us by the Military Commission, and the Consultant signed off on all business on these streets! Why should we move out just because you say so?

steps.name: Calm Woman
steps.text: Calm down, Barrel, this isn't personal. As for you, Beck, you need to watch your words.

steps.name: Broken Horn Boss
steps.text: As if I'm wrong, Ebony?

steps.name: Broken Horn Boss
steps.text: Why should these Head-Sellers be allowed to take our turf after spending so many years on the outside?

steps.name: Calm Woman
steps.text: You weren't the boss of your gang when the Consultant gave them those two blocks.

steps.name: Broken Horn Boss
steps.text: You know what, I should have kicked the old man off his seat sooner. I wouldn't have let the Head-Sellers set foot in here if I was in the room back then.

steps.name: Stern Mercenary
steps.text: Say that again, I dare you.

steps.name: Calm Woman
steps.text: Don't just stand there staring, pull them apart! You should get your mouth slapped, Beck. They were out there risking their lives for us.

steps.name: Calm Woman
steps.text: And you, Barrel, stop being such a hard-head! Beck could run his mouth all day, but none of it matters until the Consultant gets here.

steps.name: Broken Horn Boss
steps.text: Stop defending them, Ebony! Who gives a damn about the Consultant? How many men does he have? How many blades does he have?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Not as many men as you. But blades? That's hard to say.

steps.name: Calm Woman
steps.text: Consultant.

steps.name: Stern Mercenary
steps.text: Consultant!

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Consultant?!

steps.name: Broken Horn Boss
steps.text: Who's the Djall?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Oh, don't mind me, I'm just...

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: ...I'm the Consultant's assistant! I'm here to help him take minutes.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Yeah, my wrist's been hurting lately. You could take her place, if you have problem with it.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Oh, I forgot, you can't read.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Well, everyone's here. Let's get started... unless someone has something important to do.

steps.name: Calm Woman
steps.text: Not at all. We're all waiting on you to decide how to split the piece of iron.
The cloth over it is pulled away, stirring up a cloud of dust. Nymph covers her nose with the back of her hand and squints at what lay underneath.
It is a large rock that has been touched by fire and smoke, with broken Originium pieces scattered across the surface. Underneath the cracked exterior are honeycomb-shaped rust marks.
The woman, whom the others called Ebony, takes out a screwdriver and pries a small piece of rust from the crack. Light shines through the smoke upon it, reflecting a faint blue glow.
The device on Nymph's wrist trembles, as though it just felt a chill.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Looks like there's a fair bit of Oriron. Is this it?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: I think so...

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: (*whispers*) But Ermi said the detector would sound an alarm. Why is it quiet?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: The Oriron extracted from a piece this big could feed you all for a month. But who's going to extract it? All these little Originium bits on it are like mini-bombs, if not properly processed.

steps.name: Stern Mercenary
steps.text: Some of my guys had an ironworking shop on the Columbian frontier.

steps.name: Broken Horn Boss
steps.text: You'll roast it like you roast your potatoes?

steps.name: Stern Mercenary
steps.text: Shut the *Sarkaz expletive* up if you don't know what you're talking about. I can always cut it up before processing it.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: That won't work. The Originium fragments are unstable. They could go off at any time.

steps.name: Calm Woman
steps.text: We've done business with the furnace node manager over by the western wall. Should we ask him?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Didn't you understand? The fragments are unstable. You think he would risk blowing up his furnace?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Don't forget where the fireworks last night came from. If the big shots catch you, whether it's the Military Commission—

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Or the Liches, who have a slightly grim opinion of you fellas—

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: You know what's gonna happen. Not my problem if it's just your own graves that you're digging, but not when you might leave the rest of us starving.

steps.name: Calm Woman
steps.text: Is there no place in Kazdel that would take it? You're not telling us to send it back where it came from, are you?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: You're getting ahead of yourself, Ebony. We haven't gotten the Oriron out yet. Besides, just because no one will take it in Kazdel doesn't mean no one will take it out there.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Some smugglers will do anything, no matter how dangerous. You might take a hefty haircut on it, but it's better than leaving it to rot in your hands.

steps.name: Calm Woman
steps.text: How big of a haircut are we talking?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: How should I know? It's not my area of expertise. This is what I do as a consultant: I tell you how to cut the cake fairly, but I'm never the one to actually cut it.

steps.name: Broken Horn Boss
steps.text: How can we be sure the difference won't end up in your pocket?

steps.name: Calm Woman
steps.text: What are you saying, Beck? Apologize to the Consultant, now!

steps.name: Broken Horn Boss
steps.text: To him? I don't understand why you're so polite with this guy. Have things been peaceful for so long that you forgot where you should be pointing your blade?

steps.name: Broken Horn Boss
steps.text: I say he's in league with the noble masters up in the towers. He makes it so we don't get to fight or eat, so we end up fixing the walls for them!

steps.name: Broken Horn Boss
steps.text: Why would he help the Head-Sellers take my turf? I've lived in Kazdel since the day I was born. Why should I give my house to some slugs who haven't set foot here in decades?

steps.name: Stern Mercenary
steps.text: Draw your blade. Nobody's gonna say I killed an unarmed man.

steps.name: Calm Woman
steps.text: *Sarkaz expletive*, give it a rest, both of you! You can fight it out yourselves once we've got the food.

steps.name: Calm Woman
steps.text: Put your blades down, NOW!

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Ahem. I guess someone forgot what my job is.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: I just give advice. You decide to take it or not.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: I know a few smugglers, but let's just say it'd take some credit for them to handle such a hot potato.

steps.name: Calm Woman
steps.text: Sorry about Beck, Consultant. He's still young...

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: I'm not that old either, Ebony.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: I know some of you don't trust me and think that I am where I am thanks to luck alone. That's fine.

steps.name: Calm Woman
steps.text: We listen to you because you know your stuff. A full belly doesn't lie. Only greedy fools...

steps.name: Detector
steps.text: Beep! Beep!
Everyone looks in the direction of the noise to see the Djall, who claims to be the Consultant's assistant, reaching out to the piece of iron with a strange box.
She almost has it.

steps.name: Detector
steps.text: Beep—Beep—

steps.name: Detector
steps.text: Beep!

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Oh, crap, the timing...

steps.name: Stern Mercenary
steps.text: What are you doing?! Get your hand off our Oriron!

steps.name: Broken Horn Boss
steps.text: *Sarkaz expletive*, almost let you sneak it out under my nose!

steps.name: Calm Woman
steps.text: What's the deal, Consultant?

steps.name: Stern Mercenary
steps.text: I've got the door. They're not getting out.

steps.name: Broken Horn Boss
steps.text: Your rules say the penalty for stealing in this room is a lost hand, Consultant. You pick, Djall. Left or right?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: She's not stealing. I asked her to... measure the Oriron content in the rock.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Uh, that's right! It's so high, it made my detector go haywire!

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Be careful. I didn't hire you to give me a heart attack.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: S-Sorry.

steps.name: Broken Horn Boss
steps.text: I'm not sure I believe you, Consultant. You think we aren't watching you?

spans.text: I'm not sure I believe you,
You think we aren't watching you?

steps.name: Broken Horn Boss
steps.text: It's one thing to help the Head-Sellers; at least they're sticking their necks out. But working with the tower-dwellers? That's another beast.

steps.name: Broken Horn Boss
steps.text: Why would a Djall girl in a pretty dress like that work as your assistant?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: These are old clothes from my mom and dad. I just cut them to fit me...

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: That has nothing to do with what we're talking about today. The more important thing here is how we turn this piece of iron into food, isn't it?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: How about this, I'll get someone willing to go over the walls to bring some food and take away this ticking time bomb, and then you can take your time to figure out how to share the food.

steps.name: Broken Horn Boss
steps.text: I changed my mind. Food's gone once you eat it. I want blades, Oriron! Oriron, and one hand from this thief. Do we have a deal?

steps.name: Stern Mercenary
steps.text: Can you extract the Oriron?

steps.name: Calm Woman
steps.text: I won't ask about your connections, Beck. You want the piece of iron, you can have it, but you got to supply our share of the food. Do the Broken Horns have that much food?

steps.name: Broken Horn Boss
steps.text: Didn't the Consultant call this a time bomb? You want food from me when I'm helping you solve a problem?

steps.name: Stern Mercenary
steps.text: It fell in our yard. Food or Oriron, the Veteran's Home takes the biggest share.

steps.name: Broken Horn Boss
steps.text: Hah! Those streets belong to Broken Horns! You don't even get leftovers!

steps.name: Calm Woman
steps.text: We'll follow the Consultant's rules. Everyone here gets a share. The mercenaries get an additional share to repair their roof.

steps.name: Broken Horn Boss
steps.text: Why does HE get to set the rules? Why not me?

steps.name: Calm Woman
steps.text: Don't think for a second that we're scared of the Broken Horns, Beck.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: You'll be arguing for the next hundred years at this rate. If the Broken Horns want this iron so much, they can have it.

steps.name: Stern Mercenary
steps.text: Consultant...?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Let me finish. Any damages resulting from mishandling by the Broken Horns will also be Beck's responsibility.

steps.name: Broken Horn Boss
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: As for the rest of you, whether it's food or Oriron you want, I'll take care of it. Consider it an apology for the little commotion just now. You can come get your share once I've figured out the amount.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Not for free, of course. My pockets aren't that deep. Any firework pieces that fell on your turf, you bring to me, no matter how big or small.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Don't be so short-sighted. The Liches may not be roaming the streets day after day now, but they're always watching us. Make sure you understand what you're allowed to take, and what you shouldn't even go near.

steps.name: Stern Mercenary
steps.text: No objection. I picked up a lot of small pieces, but they're too small to be anything useful.

steps.name: Calm Woman
steps.text: How does this work? How much food and Oriron can we get for the pieces?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Excuse me, I have an idea... the amount of Oriron can be calculated from the purity, but I'll need to take another measurement, since I got interrupted.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: It would be best if I could take a small sample.
Pohl looks at Nymph with bewilderment in his eyes, but nods his head. The others give way for Nymph to take her peculiar hand-box to the cracked 'piece of iron'.
She takes out a strange rod and knocks on the surface lightly. A small, dull-colored piece falls out from inside.
Nymph's box opens slowly, sucking the piece in. When the box closes, everyone in the room feels compelled to look to the window.
The skies are still dark, but the light shining in seems to have gotten brighter and warmer.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Whew... done.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Write your choice of supplies and your name on the paper, and come back in three days. You know where to find me.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Doesn't matter if you can't write, Beck. You got the whole piece of iron; you're not getting anything else from me.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: And I'll deal with the territorial dispute between the mercenaries and the Broken Horns, same day, next month. All of you better show up.

steps.name: Stern Mercenary
steps.text: Here's the paper, just like you wanted, Consultant.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Anything else? Alright, you can get back to your own lives now.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Thank you so much, Consultant. You're really a huge help.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Ah, it's nothing. I've crossed paths with that Lich lady before, after all. It's the least I could do.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: And please... call me Pohl.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: I didn't expect the legendary Consultant to be so... young.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: But the supplies that you promised the people here, to get me out of that jam—do you really have so much food and Oriron in stock?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Maybe? I've stocked up a bit over the years. Not sure if it's enough, though... maybe I should get a head start on picking up the firework pieces...

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: The clothes on your back are all wet.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Really? Well, I guess it's a hot day today.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Pohl, were you... scared?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Well...

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: (Of course I was scared!)

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: (Did you see how many men they had? And how many blades? They could have eaten me for dinner if they meant it!)

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: (What was I supposed to do? I just wanted to get everybody together and make our lives a little better. How was I supposed to know that things would turn out like this?)

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: I didn't sign up to become the Consultant!

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Calm down, calm down! We're safe.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: ...You heard that?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Djaj can read minds, can't they? Did you...?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: It's okay, I didn't peek! Why does everyone think we can do that?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: It's true that I'm a little more sensitive to people's fear... but it's very demanding Arts! And do you think I really want to hear what other people are thinking?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: I guess you're right... it's not exactly pleasant stuff you would see in Kazdel.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Anyway, did you get what you needed?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Yeah. It's perfect. Look!

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: It's so small. But it does look unique.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: It was surrounded by Oriron. That's why the detector didn't react.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Well, you got what you came for, didn't you?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: No, I'm just getting started.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Ermi... my Lich friend says there's at least four or five more pieces in the city, and I have no idea where to find them. I was planning on asking someone well-connected...

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: But who's better connected in these parts than you? You must know something, right Consultant?

spans.text: But who's better connected in these parts than you? You must know something, right

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: I have a rough idea where some of the pieces might have fallen, but I can't be sure whether they'll have revenants in them or not.

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: It's a start! Better than stumbling around the city trying my luck!

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: If you help me find the remaining pieces, I'll ask the lazy Liches to reimburse the food and Oriron you're handing out!

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Well, food might be a little difficult, but Oriron shouldn't be a problem. There's always parts coming off the Furnace during maintenance!

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Well, I guess I couldn't do worse...

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Hey, stop tugging on my sleeve!

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: I'll take that as a yes! A little stroll would do you some good, given how stressed you are.

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: Who said I was stressed?

steps.name: Nymph
steps.text: Did you forget I'm a Djall?

steps.name: Pohl
steps.text: You said you didn't look!
